title: Customer Match
content:
# Customer Match

Create a Google Customer Match audience from a CRM email list with POST /v1/ads/audiences and a hashed member upload.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

By the end of this page, a CRM list is a Google Customer Match audience you can target.

## Create an audience

Create the empty `customer_list` audience with `POST /v1/ads/audiences`. Then upload members with `POST /v1/ads/audiences/{audienceId}/users`.

`adAccountId` is the Google Ads customer id (no dashes).

Google matches on email only, and any `phone` is ignored. Values are SHA-256 hashed server-side before upload.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data: created } = await zernio.adaudiences.createAdAudience({
  body: {
    accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d',
    adAccountId: '1234567890',
    type: 'customer_list',
    name: 'Newsletter subscribers'
  }
});

const { data: upload } = await zernio.adaudiences.addUsersToAdAudience({
  path: { audienceId: created.audience.id },
  body: { users: [{ email: 'jane@example.com' }, { email: 'sam@example.com' }] }
});

console.log(upload.numReceived);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

created = client.ad_audiences.create_ad_audience(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="1234567890",
    type="customer_list",
    name="Newsletter subscribers",
)

upload = client.ad_audiences.add_users_to_ad_audience(
    audience_id=created["audience"]["id"],
    users=[{"email": "jane@example.com"}, {"email": "sam@example.com"}],
)

print(upload["numReceived"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/audiences" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d", "adAccountId": "1234567890", "type": "customer_list", "name": "Newsletter subscribers" }'

curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/audiences/66e5b2c3d4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1/users" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "users": [{ "email": "jane@example.com" }, { "email": "sam@example.com" }] }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "audience": {
    "id": "66e5b2c3d4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1",
    "name": "Newsletter subscribers",
    "type": "customer_list",
    "platform": "google"
  },
  "message": "Audience created"
}
```

The create is not idempotent, so never auto-retry it.

Response (`200`):

```json
{ "message": "Users added", "numReceived": 2, "numInvalid": 0 }
```

Each upload takes up to 10,000 users.

A `200` means Google accepted the rows, not that the audience can be targeted.

Google matches the hashed emails against active Google accounts. This takes from about 10 minutes to 24 hours.

Google serves a Customer Match list only once the matched list holds enough active users at the moment the ad is served.

<Callout type="warn">
Upload at least 5,000 members to clear that threshold, per Google's own guidance ([Customer Match](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/remarketing/audience-types/customer-match)).
</Callout>

A small test list that reports `numInvalid: 0` and then never serves is that threshold, not a failed upload.

To target the audience, pass its `platformAudienceId` (from `GET /v1/ads/audiences?accountId=&adAccountId=`) in `audienceInclude` on `POST /v1/ads/create`.

## If it fails

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `422` `invalid_field_value` | The upload targets an audience that is not a `customer_list`, or has no platform id yet | Upload to a `customer_list` audience that has a platform id |
| Upload returns `200` but the list never serves | The matched list is under Google's serving threshold | Upload more members (Google's guidance is at least 5,000) |

The `422` body:

```json
{
  "error": "Audience has no platform ID. It may not have been created on the platform yet.",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "code": "invalid_field_value"
}
```
